To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the velocity fluctuations are the main driving force for the shear viscosity of non-Brownain suspensions close to the glass transition and that the statistical properties are determined by stochastical effects and are independent of the dissipation mechanism.

the velocity fluctuations of the grains control the dissipation and therefore the rheology of the system, and that these fluctuations are similar in the different numerical models, implying that the exponent of the viscosity is independent of the dissipation scheme.

the rheology of a dense suspension close to jamming is controlled by velocity fluctuations, which are similar to those of quasi-static simulations and depend on the dissipated energy only through the volume fraction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the rheology of granular materials.
the rheology of granular suspensions close to the jamming transition.
the rheology of non-Browniannon-Brownian suspending particles in the limit of vanishing inertia and vanishing thermal noise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rheology of a dense suspension close to jamming is controlled by the statistical properties of the grain trajectories.
the rheology close to jamming is controlled by velocity fluctuations, which are mainly due to the interplay of the steric forces and the finite strain rates.
the critical exponent of the viscosity is determined by the critical exponent of steric effects, and not of the velocity fluctuations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rheology of a dense suspension of non-Browninan particles can be understood from the statistical mechanics of a system with purely repulsive forces.

the rheological properties close to jamming can be described by a simple model, where the dissipation rate is determined by a power law of the velocity fluctuations, and the exponent is determined by steric interactions.
in the shear flow of non-Browian suspensions close jamming, the rheological behavior is determined by the steric forces between grains and is insensitive to the dissipation mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical exponent of the effective viscosity with respect to volume fractions is a universal quantity, and can be predicted from a simple model of steric effects.

the dynamical mechanisms controlling jamming are the same in quasistatic and dynamic calculations, and that the effective viscosity can be predicted from the statistical properties of velocity fluctuations.
, in order to understand the flow behavior of a suspension, one needs to understand its statistical mechanics, rather than its hydrodynamics.
